text.p: This work is based on Ironsworn, Ironsworn: Delve and Ironsworn: Starforged, created by Shawn Tomkin, and licensed for our use under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

This is an unofficial adaptation made for Kraken VTT, compatible with Ironsworn and Ironsworn: Starforged. It is not an official Tomkin Press product, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Shawn Tomkin or Tomkin Press. It uses no Tomkin Press art, icons or trade dress. The full rulebooks (free to download from the publisher) explain the games in far more depth.
The foes in this book are Kraken VTT's own. Delve's site themes and domains are Shawn Tomkin's (CC BY 4.0, from Datasworn).
A foe is a rank and a story. Its rank says how hard it is to beat (how much each hit marks on its track) and how badly it hurts: troublesome 1 harm, dangerous 2, formidable 3, extreme 4, epic 5.

Put foes on the combat tracker from the NPC list. In Ironsworn the tracker shows each foe's rank and its ten-box progress track instead of hit points, and each character's initiative. Use Inflict harm on a character (it makes their Endure Harm with the foe's harm), or let the players make their suffer moves themselves.
A group of weak foes can be one foe of a higher rank. A big fight can be several objectives, each with its own rank.

Ironsworn games play well with no game master. The players make the moves, ask the oracles, and decide together what the answers mean. In Kraken the host can still be a player: whoever hosts makes a character too, rolls oracles in the Oracles window and puts foes on the tracker when a fight starts.
When you are the GM, you are a guide more than an opponent: ask the players what they fear and hope, and use the oracles when you want to be surprised as well.
